rationale: Targeted check of the delivered branch diff for EPMCDME-13962 (project_budget_router.py + test_project_budget_router.py). The access change is sound: update_project_budget_group loads the group first, then authorizes on (is_admin_or_maintainer or group.project_name in user.admin_project_names) and raises 403 otherwise, so a project admin cannot reach a group outside their own project; the DB read before the decision is what prevents the scope leak. _ensure_allowed_budget_group_update_fields then restricts every non-maintainer to the categories field, and derives its restricted set from ProjectBudgetGroupUpdateRequest.model_fields minus {categories}, so any field added to the request model later is denied by default rather than silently allowed. Read paths, validation (_validate_group_categories) and the 404-instead-of-403 group-id enumeration guard on GET are unchanged. All other mutating endpoints (PATCH budget, DELETE, POST reset/rebalance/override) remain on maintainer_access_only, matching the spec's out-of-scope list. Verified live against a local backend as a user with is_admin=false, is_maintainer=false, is_auditor=false who is project admin on the target project: PUT with total_amount, name, budget_duration or description each returned 403 'Project administrators may only update the categories field.'; a mixed {total_amount + valid categories} payload was rejected whole (categories not partially applied); a categories-only payload returned 200; re-reading the group afterwards showed name, total_amount, budget_duration, description and every category max_budget/soft_budget unchanged. No blocking defect found in the delivered code. One spec acceptance criterion (audit event enrichment) is not implemented in the final branch state — recorded under business_review and risk_flags below, not as a code defect.
risk_flags: Spec AC 'PROJECT_BUDGET_GROUP_UPDATED event includes old_categories and new_categories' is not implemented in the final branch state: grep for old_categories/new_categories over src/ returns no match, and update_project_budget_group still emits attributes={'project_name': group.project_name}. Commit b928a0dc3 added this enrichment earlier in the branch; it is absent after the subsequent refactor commits. The update remains auditable (event type, entity id, actor id, project name) but without the before/after distribution values the spec asked for.

_ensure_allowed_budget_group_update_fields bypasses only on user.is_maintainer, so a platform admin (is_admin true, is_maintainer false) is also limited to categories. This matches the frontend, which grants 'full' access to maintainers only and 'distribution' to platform and project admins, so it is read as intentional rather than a defect.

business_review.criterion: Project Admin can view spend bucket distribution for budgets in their project
business_review.notes: Pre-existing _ensure_project_budget_read_access path, unchanged by this MR. Confirmed live: GET of the group returned 200 for a project admin who is not the group's creator.

business_review.criterion: Project Admin can change spend bucket distribution for budgets they administer
business_review.notes: Verified live: categories-only PUT returned 200 for a non-admin, non-maintainer project admin. Covered by test_update_group_project_admin_own_project_categories_only_succeeds.

business_review.criterion: The system validates that distribution values are correct before saving
business_review.notes: _validate_group_categories is unchanged and still runs on the project admin path; category validity, platform presence and the sum-within-0.5-of-100 tolerance all apply identically.

business_review.criterion: Unauthorized users cannot change spend bucket distribution
business_review.notes: 403 for a project admin of a different project and for users with no project admin rights; covered by the parametrized test_update_group_write_access and test_project_budget_write_routes_deny_pure_auditor.

business_review.criterion: Updated distribution is reflected in budget tracking and reporting
business_review.notes: No code change; existing provider sync path handles this and was declared out of scope in the spec. Not independently exercised in this check.

business_review.criterion: All changes are auditable: PROJECT_BUDGET_GROUP_UPDATED includes old_categories and new_categories
business_review.notes: Not present in the final branch state. src/ contains no old_categories or new_categories symbol; the event is emitted with attributes={'project_name': group.project_name} only. The event itself still records event type, entity id, actor id and project name, so the update is traceable but the before/after distribution values are missing.

business_review.criterion: Tests cover successful update by project admin, invalid distribution, cross-project unauthorized access, non-admin unauthorized access, and audit event payload
business_review.notes: Project admin success, non-categories field rejection, cross-project and non-admin denial, and auditor denial are covered in tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_project_budget_router.py. No audit-payload test, consistent with the enrichment not being implemented.

standards_review.notes: Every commit on the branch carries the EPMCDME-13962: prefix.

Duplicated access-denied literals were extracted into _ACCESS_DENIED_MESSAGE and _ACCESS_DENIED_HELP; the new helper is small, typed and documented with a one-line docstring matching the file's style.

The group is loaded and the project resolved before the authorization decision, so the project scope is derived from stored data rather than from the request. Failure mode is a 403 with a non-leaking message; GET keeps returning 404 for unauthorized group ids to prevent enumeration.

Restricted field set is computed from the request model's own fields, so it cannot drift out of date when the model grows. Confirmed by live REST probes that name, total_amount, budget_duration and description are all rejected.

follow_ups: Decide whether the dropped PROJECT_BUDGET_GROUP_UPDATED enrichment (old_categories / new_categories) is still required. If it is, restore it in update_project_budget_group before merge; if the requirement was intentionally dropped, update spec.md so the acceptance criteria match what ships.

verification.method: static review of the branch diff plus live REST probes against a local backend
verification.actor: authenticated user, is_admin=false, is_maintainer=false, is_auditor=false, project admin on the target project, not the group's creator
verification.post_state: group re-read after all probes: name, total_amount, budget_duration, description and every category max_budget/soft_budget unchanged
